source_text: Tunc Iacobo quoque in recordationem rediit quod hanc sibi significasset coronam diuinae dignationis ostensio. Nam superioribus diebus, cum eiusdem carrucae uehiculo Marianus et Iacobus et cum his ego uiam communiter carperemus, ad medium fere diem inter illa itineris confragosa mirabili et alto sopore correptus, postquam a nobis interpellatus et excitatus euigilat, Perturbatus sum, inquit, non sine gaudio meo, fratres; sed et uos mecum gaudere debetis. Uidi, inquit, iuuenem inenarrabili et satis ampla magnitudine, cuius uestitus discincta erat in tantum candida luce, ut oculi in eam constanter uidere non possent; cuius pedes terram non calcabant et uultus oris super nubes erat. Is cum transcurreret, unam tibi, Mariane, et unam mihi zonas purpureas in sinus nostros iaculatus est, et ait: Sequimini me cito. O quietem uigiliis omnibus fortiorem! O quietem quam feliciter dormiat quisquis in fide uigilat! Quae terrena tantum membra sopierat, quoniam uidere dominum nisi spiritus non ualebat. Quantum exultantes quamque sublimes animos martyrum fuisse credendum est, quibus in sancti nominis confessione passuris et audire Christum ante contigit et uidere offerentem se suis quocumque in loco, quocumque tempore. Non fuit inpedimento uehiculi se promouentis inquieta iactatio, nec dies medius, qui sub claro tunc sole fulgebat. Nulla noctis expectata secreta sunt: nouo genere gratiae martyri suo dominus nouum tempus uisionis elegit.
pass_a_gloss: Then James also came to remember that a manifestation of divine favour had marked out this crown for him; for on earlier days, while Marian and James and I along with them were travelling together in the conveyance of the same wagon, about the middle of the day among the rough stretches of the road he was seized by a wondrous deep slumber, and after being spoken to by us and roused he awakes saying he had been agitated with a joy not absent to himself and that his brothers ought to rejoice with him; he reported seeing a youth of indescribable and very large stature whose loose garment was white with so great a light that eyes could not steadily look at it, whose feet did not press the ground and whose countenance was above the clouds, who while hastening past threw one purple band into Marian's bosom and one into his own and said Follow me swiftly; an exclamation that such rest is mightier than all vigils and that happy is whoever in faith watches while so sleeping, since it had lulled only earthly limbs because only the spirit could see the Lord; a reflection on how rejoicing and exalted the martyrs' spirits must be believed to have been, since before suffering in confession of the holy name it fell to them both to hear Christ beforehand and to see him offering himself to his own in whatever place and whatever time; an assertion that neither the uneasy jolting of the advancing vehicle nor the midday then gleaming under a clear sun was a hindrance, and no secrecies of night were waited for, because by a new kind of favour the Lord selected a new season of vision for his martyr.
pass_b_english: Then it also came back to the memory of James that a disclosure of divine favour had foretold this crown to him. For on former days, when Marianus and James, and I along with them, were travelling together in the carriage of the same wagon, toward midday amid the rugged stretches of the road James was seized by a wondrous and deep slumber, and when we spoke to him and roused him he woke and said: I have been shaken, he said, yet not without my own joy, brothers; but you also ought to rejoice with me. I saw, he said, a youth of unspeakable and surpassing stature, whose ungirt garment shone white with so bright a light that eyes could not look steadily upon it; his feet did not tread the earth and his face was above the clouds. As he hastened by, he cast one purple girdle into your lap, Marianus, and one into mine, and said: Follow me swiftly. O rest mightier than all keeping awake! O rest in which he who keeps watch in faith sleeps so blessedly! It had lulled only earthly limbs to sleep, since none but the spirit had strength to see the Lord.

How exultant and how uplifted must the souls of the martyrs be believed to have been, to whom, when about to suffer in confession of the holy name, it was granted both to hear Christ beforehand and to behold him presenting himself to his own in whatever place and at whatever time. The restless tossing of the carriage moving forward was no hindrance, nor the midday hour which then blazed beneath a bright sun. No hidden hours of night were awaited: by a new manner of grace the Lord chose for his martyr a new hour for the vision.
